decision: exclude: single-shot video QA; internalized future-frame prediction is not a persistent agent belief state
note: Internalizes predictive world modeling into training (next-embedding prediction of future frames); matches Visual CoT with >5x lower latency, but no multi-step agent or revisable state.
title: Beyond Visual CoT: Internalized Visual Thinking for Proactive Video Reasoning

decision: exclude: audience ToM model for one-shot persuasive writing; no environment belief revised across decisions
note: ToM Reasoner builds a static dual model of audience beliefs/values to condition planning and retrieval; top Elo across three benchmarks, but belief is not updated by evidence across steps.
title: ARGUS: Theory-of-Mind Guided Argument Generation with Strategy-Aware Planning and Knowledge Grounding

decision: exclude: evaluation methodology (LLM-as-judge); no state or belief
note: GPT-4 judges agree with humans >80%; MT-Bench is a multi-turn question set but scores answer quality, not state tracking.

decision: include
note: Foundational output-level credit: closed-form policy from preference pairs with a classification loss; defines the 'credit to output' baseline that multi-turn agent methods extend to trajectory/state.
title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

decision: include
note: Single LM learns to decide when evidence is needed and to critique retrieved passages via reflection tokens; 7B/13B outperform ChatGPT on open-domain QA and fact verification. Lineage for evidence-acquisition-on-demand, but single-turn.

decision: exclude: single-turn RL optimizer (GRPO variant) for math reasoning; no multi-turn state

title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale

decision: exclude: single-prompt inference scaling; no persistent state

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters

decision: exclude: single-turn RL optimizer analysis; no multi-turn state
note: Identifies GRPO length bias and proposes Dr. GRPO (43.3% AIME 2024 with 7B); background for GRPO-family baselines only.
title: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective

decision: exclude: GUI perception/grounding VLM; no explicit state or belief
note: 18B VLM with high-resolution encoder reaches SOTA on Mind2Web and AITW from screenshots alone; per-step action prediction without state maintenance.
title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents

decision: exclude: single-turn RL optimizer; sequence-level importance ratio, no multi-turn state
note: Sequence-level importance ratios and clipping stabilize MoE RL vs GRPO; cite only as the sequence-level credit unit in Section 5 if needed.
title: Group Sequence Policy Optimization

decision: exclude: single-turn program synthesis with a critic; no persistent state
note: Actor-critic RL with a critic predicting functional correctness gives dense token-level credit for code; SOTA on APPS. Early example of critic-shaped credit but not multi-turn.
title: CodeRL: Mastering Code Generation through Pretrained Models and Deep Reinforcement Learning

decision: exclude: robot task-and-motion planning with feasibility Q-functions; no maintained belief state

title: Text2Motion: from natural language instructions to feasible plans

decision: exclude: web agent architecture (planning + HTML summarization); no explicit state

title: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis

decision: include
revision_signal: edited fact stored externally; iterative prompting checks generated answers against stored edits
belief_level_metrics: yes: multi-hop accuracy after edit (ripple-effect consistency)
note: Editing one fact should ripple to entailed beliefs: current editors recall the edited fact but fail catastrophically on multi-hop questions; MeLLo (external edit memory + iterative consistency prompting) outperforms them by a large margin. Lineage for belief-revision consistency failure modes.
title: MQuAKE: Assessing Knowledge Editing in Language Models via Multi-Hop Questions
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

decision: exclude: plan-then-execute efficiency for tool use; no state maintained or revised on observations
revision_signal: none (reasoning decoupled from observations by design)
note: Decoupling reasoning from observations yields 5x token efficiency and +4% on HotpotQA; useful as the 'no observation-driven revision' contrast to ReAct, but not itself a belief method.
title: ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models

decision: exclude: action-candidate generation for text games; no explicit belief state
note: LM trained on human gameplay proposes action candidates re-ranked by an RL agent; 69% relative gain on Jericho. Pre-LLM text-game lineage but state is implicit.
title: Keep CALM and Explore: Language Models for Action Generation in Text-based Games
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

decision: exclude: data unification pipeline for agent SFT; no state or credit method
note: Unifies heterogeneous multi-turn trajectories for agent training and releases xLAM-v0.1; engineering contribution only.
title: AgentOhana: Design Unified Data and Training Pipeline for Effective Agent Learning

decision: include
revision_signal: TD-loss update of a learned belief network over co-agent strategies (belief embedding from local history)
note: Recasts multi-LLM coordination as an incomplete-information game: each execution LLM keeps a belief-state embedding about co-agents (trained by TD loss) and receives an individual trajectory-level reward (action-likelihood + task + collaborative contribution); +11.2% over debate on six benchmarks with 21.4% fewer tokens. Belief is over other agents, not the environment.
title: From Debate to Equilibrium: Belief-Driven Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning via Bayesian Nash Equilibrium

decision: include
revision_signal: in-context evidence pieces presented within conversation history
belief_level_metrics: yes: Bayesian Coherence Coefficient (correlation of expected vs observed log-odds updates)
note: Defines BCC = Corr(expected LLR update, observed log-odds change) on 6,460 (class pair, evidence, history) tuples; BCC correlates with log parameter count at r=0.906 across five model families, all models > 0. A belief-level revision metric in context, without an acting agent.
title: Are LLM Belief Updates Consistent with Bayes' Theorem?
evidence: P (ICML 2025 Workshop on Assessing World Models)

decision: exclude: single-turn forecasting calibration; no persistent state carried between decisions
note: Forecasting accuracy and calibration vary sharply with domain, question type, and added news context; belief formation studied one question at a time.
title: Future Is Unevenly Distributed: Forecasting Ability of LLMs Depends on What We're Asking

decision: exclude: off-domain (speech understanding); latent-state world model not tied to an LLM agent acting over steps
note: Factorizes speech understanding into four modules over a causal graph with forward dynamics over latent states; interpretability contribution, no decision agent.
title: Speech World Model: Causal State-Action Planning with Explicit Reasoning for Speech

decision: exclude: within-response answer commitment; no persistent cross-decision state
belief_level_metrics: proxy: finite-answer log-odds stabilization time (17-31 token lead)
note: Projected log-odds over a finite answer set stabilize 17-31 tokens before the parseable answer in Qwen3-4B; tracks the model's eventual output rather than truth. Possible pointer for implicit-belief representation but single-turn.
title: When Does a Language Model Commit? A Finite-Answer Theory of Pre-Verbalization Commitment

decision: exclude: off-domain social simulation of networked belief formation; no agent state maintenance method
note: Networks of LLM agents approximate human group coherence on sanitized hashtag tasks but need structured prompting for politically sensitive narratives.
title: Simulating hashtag dynamics with networked groups of generative agents
venue: International Conference on Advances in Social Networks Analysis and Mining

decision: exclude: off-domain single-turn classification benchmark
note: Nine LLMs on a real-world scam dataset; prompting boosts small models and LLMs generalize better than fine-tuned BERT. Unrelated to belief state.
title: Measuring and Evaluating the Performance of Generative Ai Models for Scam Detection
venue: Annual International Computer Software and Applications Conference

decision: exclude: off-domain ethical introspection via prompt scaffolding; no environment or decision loop; abstract only
revision_signal: detected belief contradiction triggers five-phase introspection and revised beliefs
belief_level_metrics: proxy: belief continuity / logical consistency rated by humans (kappa 0.81)
note: Prompt-only GPT-4 Turbo scaffold with a symbolic belief structure and reflective memory log revises contradictory beliefs; evaluated by five subjective introspection metrics with inter-rater kappa 0.81. Abstract only; no arXiv id.
title: Integrating Neural and Symbolic Paradigms for Reflective Ethical Reasoning and Belief Modeling
venue: 2026 International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)

decision: exclude: retrieval-augmented pretraining for open-QA; no belief or uncertainty condition
note: Latent knowledge retriever trained end-to-end with MLM; +4-16% absolute on Open-QA. Pure retrieval lineage.
title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training

decision: exclude: grounding study for multimodal web agents; no explicit state
note: GPT-4V completes 51.1% of live-website tasks with oracle grounding; grounding, not belief, is the bottleneck studied.
title: GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded

decision: exclude: end-to-end multimodal web agent and task-success benchmark; no state tracking metric
note: 59.1% task success on 15 real websites with GPT-4V auto-evaluation at 85.3% human agreement; scores outcomes only.
title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

decision: exclude: retrieval memory (KG + Personalized PageRank) for multi-hop QA; no belief or uncertainty condition
note: Hippocampal-indexing-inspired KG retrieval beats RAG baselines by up to 20% on multi-hop QA at 10-30x lower cost than IRCoT; static knowledge integration, not agent belief.
title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models

decision: exclude: GUI agent using action history as context; no explicit state
note: Chain-of-action (previous actions + future plan) gives 90% action-type accuracy and 74% action success on AITW; history is implicit context only.
title: You Only Look at Screens: Multimodal Chain-of-Action Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

decision: include
belief_level_metrics: proxy: transition-modeling F1 on predicted preconditions/effects and planner success; error taxonomy (hallucination, affordance, planning)
note: Formalizes four LLM modules incl. transition modeling (predict PDDL preconditions/effects) with logic-matching F1 and planner success; Claude-3.5 gets 78.8% F1 on object states but 58.6% on spatial relations, o1-preview 90.2% planner success on BEHAVIOR; LLMs overstate effects and understate preconditions. A benchmark of the agent's world model.
title: Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making

decision: exclude: web navigation agent (HTML simplification + curriculum + RL/rejection sampling); no explicit state
note: ChatGLM3-6B web agent trained with curriculum SFT, RL and rejection sampling; releases AutoWebBench. Outcome-level credit, no belief.
title: AutoWebGLM: A Large Language Model-based Web Navigating Agent

decision: include
revision_signal: user preference stated explicitly or implicitly earlier in conversation
belief_level_metrics: proxy: preference-following accuracy over turns (memory validity of user state)
note: 3,000 preference/query pairs over 20 topics in multi-session conversations up to 100k tokens; zero-shot preference following drops below 10% at just 10 turns (~3k tokens) for most of 10 models, RAG and prompting still degrade with length, fine-tuning helps. Measures persistence of a user-state claim across decisions.
title: Do LLMs Recognize Your Preferences? Evaluating Personalized Preference Following in LLMs

decision: include
revision_signal: memory lifecycle scheduling: MemCubes with provenance and versioning composed, migrated, fused over time
note: Treats memory as an OS-managed resource unifying plaintext, activation and parameter memories in versioned MemCubes with provenance; a representation-level proposal for memory evolution, without belief-level evaluation in the abstract.
title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System

decision: include
belief_level_metrics: proxy: memory effectiveness, efficiency and capacity across factual vs reflective memory levels
note: Benchmark of LLM-agent memory with factual and reflective levels and participation vs observation scenarios, scored on effectiveness, efficiency and capacity; no headline numbers in abstract.
title: MemBench: Towards More Comprehensive Evaluation on the Memory of LLM-based Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

decision: include
revision_signal: none (state is screenshot history in context)
note: Asynchronous distributed online RL for Android control with A-RIDE: sparse AI-evaluator terminal reward plus step penalties, step-level advantages from a value classifier with trajectory-level filtering and Retrace(lambda) off-policy correction; 3x training efficiency and 73.2% vs 61.2% success over DigiRL. Credit flows to trajectory/steps, not to state.
title: DistRL: An Asynchronous Distributed Reinforcement Learning Framework for On-Device Control Agents

decision: include
revision_signal: LLM emits memory-write of extracted triplets; updatable, aggregatable store queried on demand
note: Early explicit read-write triplet memory unit for LLMs (Davidsonian triplets), updatable and interpretable, with qualitative gains on temporal QA; lineage for written external memory. Credit: imitation of memory API calls only.
title: RET-LLM: Towards a General Read-Write Memory for Large Language Models

decision: include
revision_signal: accumulated simulated user feedback during service time
belief_level_metrics: proxy: continual-learning gains from accumulated feedback (effectiveness and efficiency)
note: User-feedback simulation framework and multi-domain, multilingual benchmark for memory and continual learning in LLM systems; SOTA memory baselines are 'far from satisfying' at learning from service-time feedback.
title: MemoryBench: A Benchmark for Memory and Continual Learning in LLM Systems
